title: Wren and the Well
premise: When Felix Brightwater returns to the drought-stricken town of Hollowmere to bury his twin sister Wren, he discovers the body in the casket is not hers — and Wren may have been taken by something beneath the old well that the town's founding families sealed generations ago. As an excavation crew breaches a door sealed from the inside, Felix's obsessive documentation becomes the only weapon against an entity that rewrites memory and identity, trading truth for loyalty. To save Wren, Felix must expose what the founders invited in, hold out until sunrise when the entity's 'contracts' lapse, and convince the last living signatory to refuse renewal — even if refusing means the town must finally grieve its buried crimes. The story ends at dawn: the papers burn, Wren walks out of the dark half-changed, and Felix chooses to publish the truth rather than keep it as a private prayer.
about_author: Ada Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist from the Karoo who spent a decade cataloguing estate papers in houses nobody wanted to enter. She writes horror about paperwork, grief, and the things families agree not to know.

chapters.title: The Wrong Body
chapters.summary: Felix arrives in Hollowmere for Wren's funeral and insists on viewing the body — a habit of verification he can't shake. The face in the casket is Wren's, but the hands are wrong: calloused, older, one fingernail torn as if from digging. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dread disguised as grief; the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Felix catalogs the funeral, the mourners' rehearsed condolences, and the odd absence of anyone from the Vane family, whose name appears on the oldest gravestones. He photographs everything, including a wet trail leading from the cemetery toward the dry well field. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: compulsive control masking terror.

chapters.title: The Crew That Came for Water
chapters.summary: Introduce the excavation crew hired to drill new wells during the drought: foreman Odile Sarr, driller Cass, and young surveyor Tam, each with debts binding them to the job. They mention the old Brightwater well was flagged on no map at all. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: pragmatic people ignoring a bad feeling because rent is due.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: In the town archive, Felix finds the 1897 Brightwater ledger: payments made monthly 'to the resident below,' signed by successive family heads. The final signature is his grandfather's — and the payments never stopped; they were simply rerouted through the town council. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of inherited complicity.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: The crew's drill breaks through a stone door forty feet down — hinges on the far side, bolted shut from within. Odile orders them up, but Cass descends anyway and comes back wrong-footed, describing a corridor 'that remembers walking.' POV: Cass. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into violation.

chapters.title: Wren's Room, Unchanged
chapters.summary: Felix searches Wren's abandoned house and finds her own documentation: audio tapes of her investigating the well before her disappearance, her voice counting footsteps that don't match the hallway's length. The last tape ends mid-sentence with a second set of breathing. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: hope and horror braided together — she was close, then she was gone.

chapters.title: The Town That Agreed Not to Know
chapters.summary: Odile confronts the mayor about the door and is met with practiced blankness; every official document about the well field is stamped with a seal shaped like a keyhole. Tam notices residents water their lawns at night from hoses connected to nothing. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: institutional gaslighting; justice will not come through channels.

chapters.title: Cass Stops Sleeping
chapters.summary: Cass begins dreaming in the corridor's geometry and wakes with dirt under her nails matching the soil from below. She signs a work order she doesn't remember reading; the ink is still wet each morning. POV: Cass. Emotional beat: identity eroding — the entity negotiates through exhaustion and debt.

chapters.title: The Last Signatory
chapters.summary: Felix traces the ledger's current signer to Marigold Vane, ninety-one, lucid and unrepentant in a house full of salt lines. She explains the arrangement: the resident below grants the town water and forgetfulness; the signatory renews the contract each generation at sunrise or sunset. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the banality of evil — an old woman doing bookkeeping for a monster.

chapters.title: It Offers You What You're Missing
chapters.summary: Tam, drowning in student debt, is approached by a voice in the drill shed offering a life where the debt never existed — if he'll carry the renewal papers down. He almost signs. Odile catches him with pen in hand. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: temptation rendered mundane; loyalty bought cheaply.

chapters.title: The Twin Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: DNA results come back: the body in the casket shares Felix's DNA — it is, impossibly, another version of Wren, aged decades. Marigold confirms the resident 'keeps what it likes and returns what it's finished with.' POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief destabilized into something worse — Wren may be alive, changed, or both.

chapters.title: Everything Documented Is Protected
chapters.summary: Felix discovers his photos and tapes degrade overnight unless duplicated and witnessed by someone else — the entity can rewrite solitary records but not shared testimony. He recruits Odile, Cass, and Tam as witnesses, turning his prayer into a pact. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: loneliness becoming alliance; truth needs company.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Inward
chapters.summary: At dusk the stone door stands open, and the corridor exhales cold air smelling of the cemetery. Cass, half-claimed already, walks toward it; Odile physically drags her back as the crew realizes the excavation site has become the front line. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: protective fury — the crew stops being employees and becomes a family under siege.

chapters.title: Minutes of the Founders' Meeting
chapters.summary: Felix uncovers the original 1897 minutes: the founders didn't stumble onto the resident — they invited it, trading a child (a Brightwater twin) for an end to a killing drought. Every generation since has paid in twins. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes — loyalty to family built on an unspeakable injustice.

chapters.title: Wren Below
chapters.summary: Through the open door, Felix hears Wren's voice — older, doubled, reciting the ledger entries she's been forced to memorize. She is alive, serving as the resident's amanuensis, signing nothing herself but preparing the papers others sign. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: rescue mission ignited, complicated by fear of what she's become.

chapters.title: The Renewal at Sunset
chapters.summary: Marigold dies peacefully at sundown, contract unsigned, and the town's taps run black. Panic floods Hollowmere; the council begs the crew to send someone down with fresh papers. Tam volunteers before Odile can stop him. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: the town chooses the devil it knows; betrayal wearing the mask of civic duty.

chapters.title: Descent With Witnesses
chapters.summary: Felix, Odile, and Cass go down after Tam, carrying duplicates of every documented crime the founders committed — evidence, they hope, that voids consent obtained by fraud. The corridor reshapes around their fears; only spoken, witnessed truths keep the walls honest. POV: alternating Felix/Odile. Emotional beat: solidarity as literal survival mechanism.

chapters.title: The Signing Room
chapters.summary: They find Tam at a desk of human bone, pen in hand, and Wren beside him — hollow-eyed, fluent in the resident's language of contracts. Felix reads the founders' minutes aloud, forcing the resident to hear its own origin: it was invited by liars, and fraud vitiates every renewal since. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: climax begins — truth wielded as exorcism.

chapters.title: What the Resident Wants
chapters.summary: The resident reveals itself through Wren's mouth: it doesn't want worship, only a willing signatory — someone who chooses it freely, knowing everything. It offers Felix Wren's freedom in exchange for his signature. Cass, still half-claimed, whispers that she believes him. POV: Cass. Emotional beat: the ultimate test of loyalty vs. truth — love offered as the price of silence.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Felix refuses — not heroically but precisely, citing the fraudulent invitation clause while Odile and Cass witness aloud, timestamps running. Tam tears the renewal papers; the bone desk splinters. The resident, bound by its own contractual nature, cannot act without consent, and dawn is coming. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: redemption through refusal; justice outside the law, inside the word.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: As light reaches the corridor, the contracts ignite and the resident unravels into the drought it always was — a hunger given paperwork. Wren collapses into Felix's arms, decades stolen but herself, mostly. The four climb out into a town waking to full memory and full horror. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: catharsis; the cost tallied honestly.

chapters.title: Publish Everything
chapters.summary: Weeks later, rain falls on Hollowmere for the first time in years. Felix publishes the complete record — ledgers, tapes, testimonies — rather than sealing it away like his ancestors, and Wren begins the slow work of reclaiming her lost years. Some townsfolk never forgive them for the truth. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: resolution — truth chosen over comfortable loyalty, grief begun at last.
